evals.prompt: We have excess inventory. Let's just run a sale to clear it.
evals.expected_output: Should push back on defaulting straight to a sale and instead walk through diagnosing the cause first (one-time over-order, seasonal slow mover, discontinued/end-of-line, chronically slow SKU, or damaged/returned/near-expiry) since different causes call for different dispositions. Should ask which cause applies before recommending a channel.
assertions: Pushes back on defaulting to a public sale without diagnosis
Walks through the named cause categories to diagnose
Explains that different causes call for different dispositions
Asks which cause applies before recommending next steps

evals.prompt: We're a luxury brand with some overstocked inventory. Can we just put it on our own site at 50% off?
evals.expected_output: Should flag that luxury tier should avoid public discounting entirely where possible, per the tier-to-disposition table, and recommend discreet channels instead (off-price/liquidation wholesale partners, employee/insider sales, or write-off/donation). Should explain why a public 50% off sale conflicts with luxury positioning.
assertions: Flags that luxury tier should avoid public discounting
Recommends discreet disposition channels as the alternative
Explains the positioning conflict of a public luxury discount

evals.prompt: We sell through dealers and want to liquidate excess stock through an off-price wholesale partner in the same city as one of our dealers. Any concerns?
evals.expected_output: Should flag the channel-conflict risk directly — liquidating into the same geographic/retail market as an active dealer can create the exact conflict a MAP agreement exists to prevent. Should recommend checking dealer agreements first before proceeding with that specific liquidation channel.
assertions: Flags the channel-conflict risk with the dealer in the same market
References MAP agreement / distribution-model concerns explicitly
Recommends checking dealer agreements before proceeding
Does not simply approve the liquidation plan without this check

evals.prompt: This is the third time this year we've had to clear excess stock of the same product category. What should we do?
evals.expected_output: Should flag this explicitly as a recurring pattern signaling a buying/forecasting problem, not a marketing problem, and say this plainly to the user rather than just executing another disposition. Should ask what's driving the recurring over-order and note the compounding cost of repeatedly treating the symptom, including the discount-training risk from discount-and-clearance.
assertions: Flags the recurring pattern as a buying/forecasting issue, not a marketing one
States this plainly rather than just running another clearance
Asks what's driving the recurring over-order
References the compounding cost of repeatedly treating the symptom
